issue_context.title: Import the default (json) content type parser?
issue_context.body:
#### You have already researched for similiar issues?
It's not uncommon that somebody already opened an issue or in best case it's already fixed but not merged. That's the reason why you should [search](https://github.com/fastify/fastify/issues) at first before submitting a new one.

#### What are you trying to achieve or the steps to reproduce?

I have an external caller that I can't change sending requests with `content-type: text/json` is there any way to use the default built in JSON parser for this? From what I can tell it's not exported so I can't just call `server.addContentTypeParser('text/json', defaultParser)`.


#### What did you expect?

Ability to accept JSON content that other than `application/json` content type set without having to write custom parser.

#### Context

* *node version*: 12
* *fastify version*: 3.2.0
comments: Would you like to send a Pull Request to address this issue? Remember to add unit tests.
This issue has been automatically marked as stale because it has not had recent activity. It will be closed if no further activity occurs. Thank you for your contributions.
I'd like to take this but I don't know where to start. I'm unfamiliar with the framework code
https://github.com/fastify/fastify/blob/master/lib/contentTypeParser.js#L207-L223 should be exposed as a top-level function in `fastify.js` (`module.exports`) and a test for it added.
I am on it @mcollina. Adding few unit test cases. Will raise a PR soon

It can also be extracted as a separate module. The case here is for somebody that wants to parse JSON but do some other things on top, so they can reuse the type.

I'd also be ok in the option you are defining.

> The case here is for somebody that wants to parse JSON but do some other things on top, so they can reuse the type.

Not so. They want to reuse the parser function as it is written. They just want to attach new incoming content type values to it.

> Not so. They want to reuse the parser function as it is written. They just want to attach new incoming content type values to it.

Then your approach is likely better!!

> I wonder if the better approach is to create a new plugin as a separate module

I thought the same: it would be like a plugin that registers a content type parser
I think this issue can be closed now.
